Explain how a VPN works in simple words
7:32 AM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it in scrambled form, so people on the way can't read it.

Here is how it goes:

Your device scrambles (encrypts) your data and sends it to the VPN company's computer.
That computer unscrambles it and passes it on to the website you asked for.
The website sees the VPN's address, not yours, and the reply comes back the same way.

It helps on public Wi-Fi, since strangers on the same network can't snoop. It also hides your location from websites. It doesn't make you anonymous, though, because the VPN company can still see where you go, so pick one you trust.
